data.name: The Fall of Lazarus
data.detailed_description:
You are a crew member of the USSC Lazarus waking up from cryo sleep without memories and even without name in an apparently abandoned drifting cargo spaceship. But you’re not alone, there is also Hybris, the Artificial intelligence who commands the ship. Who are you? What are you doing there? What is the Black Cube?

The Truth Is Darker Than Space.

WELCOME TO THE USSC LAZARUS


The game takes place aboard the USSC Lazarus (Unified Space Ship Companies), a ship that belongs to KR Corporation (Kross-Rübel), a company dedicated to the interstellar transport of goods and with close ties to the mining industry. The player takes on the role of the protagonist, a veteran of the Venusian wars looking to carve out a new future for herself. She has enlisted to participate in an nine-year mission to work on a mining colony. When she wakes up from hypersleep she finds herself alone on the ship and with no memories.

The player must then explore, investigate and find a way to get off the ship before the situation gets worse. Along the way, the protagonist will experience a series of traumatic events related to his personal life: visions, dreamlike recollections, strange noises and apparitions that mess with his head and make her question what is real and what is not.

We have a script with a main plot and a linear emotive journey waiting for you, but this is just the beginning. If you go deep and investigate you'll see there ir more beneath the surface. Once you've played the first scenes of the game you'll be able of wandering the full ship, searching and exploring every single detail.

The mystery of what is happening is the basis of the Lazarus gameplay, although the player is the one who gathers all the clues and details scattered throughout the ship to reach the conclusion.

FEATURES


· INMERSIVE STORYTELLING FULL OF MYSTERIES to unveil in a science fiction set up with a multi-level funcional script.
· UNCOMPRESSED NARRATIVE where there is more than meets the eye and every detail is there for a reason.
· A bunch of DIVERSE PUZZLES to solve. Logical and mechanical puzzles and social hacking.
· Powered by UNREAL ENGINE 4

reviews.review:
The Fall of Lazarus is a first person sci fi mystery game where I wake up from cryo sleep aboard the USSC Lazarus with no memories and almost no idea what is going on. The ship is supposed to be carrying out a long mining mission, but it is completely deserted. The only thing still running is Hybris, the ship's artificial intelligence, and figuring out what happened becomes the main reason I kept exploring.

The atmosphere is easily the strongest part for me. The Lazarus is a huge abandoned cargo ship, and walking through the empty rooms while hearing strange noises and slowly finding out what happened creates a really lonely feeling. The game does a good job making me curious about what is around the next corner without relying on constant enemies or cheap jumpscares.

The story is also where most of the game gets its strength. I slowly find documents, messages and other clues scattered around the ship, while visions and strange memories start making me question what I am actually experiencing. I like that the game expects me to pay attention instead of explaining absolutely everything through constant dialogue. There is a lot of information hidden around the ship if I am willing to investigate properly.

The puzzles give the exploration something to do as well. There are logical and mechanical puzzles along with some social hacking sections, so I am not just walking from one room to another. Some of them are fairly straightforward, while others made me stop and actually think about what I had already discovered.

My biggest problem is the technical side. The game was released in 2017 and the developers later explained that they were unable to continue supporting it because they had run out of money and resources. They also acknowledged that the game still had bugs and compatibility problems because there was not enough testing before release. That is pretty noticeable when I am playing it, especially when something does not behave quite how I expect.

The pacing can also be slow. I spend a lot of time walking around the ship, reading things and looking for the next clue, so there are stretches where not much seems to happen. I actually like slow atmospheric games, but I think some parts could have been tighter because the mystery sometimes loses momentum.

I still think the setting and story are worth experiencing though. There is something interesting about exploring the Lazarus and gradually putting together what happened to the crew and to the main character. The game is not particularly long or polished, but the central mystery kept me interested enough to keep looking for answers.

Overall, The Fall of Lazarus is a rough but interesting sci fi mystery that has a much stronger atmosphere and story than its technical problems would suggest. I really like the abandoned ship setting, the hidden clues and the psychological side of the story, while the bugs and slow pacing definitely hold it back. It feels like a game with a lot of ambition that never quite got the final polish it needed, but I still think there is something worth finding here.

Rating: 7.3/10
